text:
anya: quick split-bench update — ran marlin-7B on eu-west1 (H100) and us-west2 (RTX A6000) with fp16 / fp8_e4m3 / int8_dynamic profiles. posting highlights + a small csv.
chen: awesome, drop the TL;DR first pls — p50/p95 + tokens/s per gpu
anya: TL;DR: H100 fp16 p50=28ms p95=95ms tokens/s~4200; H100 fp8 p50=22ms p95=82ms tokens/s~5200 (+24%); RTX A6000 fp16 p50=46ms p95=170ms tokens/s~1800; RTX A6000 int8 p50=35ms p95=140ms tokens/s~2600 (+44% vs fp16 on RTX).
marc: nice. what about quality delta? any EM/accuracy regression on our QA eval?
anya: ran dev QA set (3.2k pairs). changes vs fp16 baseline:
- fp8_e4m3: EM drop 0.6% (95.4 -> 94.8)
- int8_dynamic: EM drop 1.7% (95.4 -> 93.7)
- fp16 baseline: 95.4
katie: 0.6% drop for fp8 seems acceptable for many prod flows, esp for 25% perf win. curious about variance across prompt lengths?
anya: split by seq len buckets (32/128/512): fp8 is stable at 32/128, small loss at 512 (~1.2% EM). int8 shows bigger variance at 512 (~3.4%).
sre-josh: any kernel fallbacks or special flags used? we saw some instabilities last week with int8 on h100.
anya: used default runtime kernel set + `cuda_mha_v2` on H100; on RTX A6000 used `cuda_mha_compat` fallback. also enabled progressive kv cache.
chen: can you paste the exact commands? want to reproduce locally
anya: sure — config snippet:
```
# run.sh snippet
MODEL=marlin-7b
PROFILES=(fp16 fp8_e4m3 int8_dynamic)
KERNELS=(cuda_mha_v2 cuda_mha_v2 cuda_mha_compat)
for p in "${PROFILES[@]}"; do
  ./bench --model $MODEL --profile $p --kernel ${KERNELS[$i]} --seq-len 512 --batch 1 --tokens 2048
done
```
marc: thanks. did you run with continuous batching on H100? could explain the better tokens/s
anya: yes H100 runs had cont-batching=on (default), RTX runs were single-request microbench to avoid memory fragmentation; that explains majority of perf gap.
katie: any memory / instability flags for int8? saw OOM on RTX if batch>2.
anya: int8 required `--force-split-gemm` on RTX to avoid OOM. didn't need that on H100.
infra-bot: deploy:bench-collector finished: results uploaded to s3://redwood-experiments/marlin7b/splitbench/1987654321/results.csv :white_check_mark:
chen: can you paste the CSV head here? just the important cols
anya: CSV head:
```
region,gpu,profile,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_s,em
eu-west1,H100,fp16,28,95,4200,95.4
eu-west1,H100,fp8_e4m3,22,82,5200,94.8
us-west2,A6000,fp16,46,170,1800,95.4
us-west2,A6000,int8_dynamic,35,140,2600,93.7
```
marc: useful. proposal: for production we can flip to fp8 on H100 for non-critical QA paths; keep fp16 for high-precision usages and int8 only for throughput-burst endpoints behind fallback.
sre-josh: for capacity planning — if we need 10k tokens/s sustained for EU, that's ~3 H100s (5200 each fp8). add 1 warm spare for canary.
katie: +1 agree. any anomalous tail latency events in the logs?
anya: one outlier run on H100 fp8 had p99=410ms due to GC pause in the host process (we traced to telemetry upload). excluding that p99 ~ 180ms.
chen: next steps?
anya: (1) run longer 24h stability on fp8 H100 with cont-batching, (2) run int8 stress test on RTX with `--force-split-gemm` and batch=2, (3) add eval on adversarial prompt set to measure quality cliff.
marc: sounds good. assign owners?
anya: I'll own (1) and (3). chen takes (2). infra-bot schedule:job assigned to @anya @chen
katie: thanks — great data. please keep the s3 link updated with plots (latency CDF + tokens/s heatmap) :bar_chart:
anya: will do, uploading perf plots tonight.
